notes: Three things here are Basque and not a translation of a neighbour. FIRST, the numeric date runs BIG-ENDIAN: 2026/01/05, year first with slashes, is the standard Basque order, while Spanish writes 05/01/2026 and French 05/01/2026 — the same country, two languages, opposite direction. SECOND, monthsInDate is NOT the same array as months, and that is the whole reason the field exists: inside a written date the month goes into the genitive, so January is urtarrila on its own but urtarrilaren the fifth — 2026ko urtarrilaren 5a. THIRD, the year and the day carry suffixes of their own: the year takes -ko (2026ko) and the day number takes the article -a (5a), which is why the LL pattern has two bracketed literals. Month and weekday names are LOWER CASE. weekdays is Sunday-first because the formatter wants it that way, while date/weekday.txt in the pack is Monday-first as a Basque speaker lists them, and the Basque week does start on Monday. Time is 24-hour with a colon (14:30). The decimal separator is a comma and the euro follows the number after a space: 1.234,56 €. Both sides of the Basque Country use the euro.
